clippings.speaker: John Wayne
clippings.quote: "I think [Ford] would have been the finest painter in the country," he said, "because he knew how to use his paint. His people, his compositions were all magnificent…"
clippings.title: What Made John Ford So Special, According To John Wayne
clippings.context: Asked by Jim Whaley in 1976 what set Ford apart from other directors; the original interview outlet is not named in the reprint, so this is secondhand.

clippings.speaker: John Wayne
clippings.quote: "I know he planned it that way. He has a way of picking on actors when they're not too important a part of a scene in order to get them on their toes. So, they'll come in ready when they really have something to do, and then he handles you like a baby."
clippings.title: Why John Wayne And John Ford Briefly Clashed On The Set Of Stagecoach
clippings.context: Wayne, asked whether Ford was deliberately riding him on the Stagecoach set, in Peter Bogdanovich's documentary Directed by John Ford; quoted from a SlashFilm clip transcription, so secondhand.

clippings.speaker: John Wayne
clippings.quote: "it's just a wonderful picture. You got great performances out of everyone, and it has a raw brutalness without any pettiness or meanness."
clippings.title: What Made John Ford So Special, According To John Wayne
clippings.context: Wayne's letter to Ford after seeing The Searchers, as quoted by SlashFilm; a private letter, so secondhand.

clippings.speaker: John Ford
clippings.quote: "God knows I want you for the picture, but you mustn’t do it as a sacrifice to yourself," Ford wrote. "… You have been doing that for me for too many years."
clippings.title: Duke's Pal, John Ford
clippings.context: Ford's letter of December 7, 1955, telling Wayne not to take a film as a sacrifice to their friendship; quoted from a John Wayne Enterprises article that cites the John Wayne Archives, so secondhand.

notes: Only four quotes; Ford-to-Wayne is thin (one letter).
